record.field: Changes effective July 1, 2026, Prince Edward Island; K1P of Prince Edward Island and its Option 2 table; tables 8.1 and 8.2

New bracket of 20% above 200,000 for 2026 and subsequent years, withheld at the prorated rate of 21% (KP 10,464) from the first pay of July 2026; the Option 2 table gives the annual 20% (KP 8,464). Basic personal amount 15,000 unchanged.
Changes effective January 1, 2026, Prince Edward Island; tables 8.1 (revised May 2026) and 8.2

Prince Edward Island rates 9.5%, 13.47%, 16.6%, 17.62% and 19% from 33,928, 65,820, 106,890 and 142,520, constants KP 1,347, 3,407, 4,497 and 6,464; the fifth threshold and its constant carry the note "*Updated May 2026". Basic personal amount 15,000 (14,650 in 2025), not indexed.
TD1PE 2026 Prince Edward Island Personal Tax Credits Return
Line 1 (basic personal amount) and the total claim amount
Prince Edward Island basic personal amount of 15,000 for 2026 and the total claim amount TCP entered on the contract.
Income Tax Act, RSPEI 1988, c. I-1
Section 7 (rates, as amended by S.P.E.I. 2026, c. 12) and s. 9(1)(c) (basic personal amount); consolidation current to May 29, 2026

For the 2026 and subsequent taxation years: 9.50% up to 33,928, 13.47% to 65,820, 16.60% to 106,890, 17.62% to 142,520, 19.00% to 200,000 and 20.00% above 200,000; basic personal amount 15,000. The path of the consolidated PDF changes with each consolidation: check its "Current to" date.
Prince Edward Island Department of Finance
Rates and brackets of the Prince Edward Island personal income tax. Prince Edward Island levies no employer payroll tax.

The page answers an automated client with a browser verification challenge instead of its content. Confirm in a browser the 2026 brackets (19% from 142,520, 20% above 200,000) and that the Department lists no employer payroll or health tax.
Workers Compensation Board of Prince Edward Island

Assessment rates set each year by the Board per $100 of assessable payroll up to the maximum assessable earnings (MAE) of the year, 89,300 for 2026, by industry rate group and adjusted by experience rating; the employer learns its rate each January in the registration renewal package.
Workers Compensation Board of Prince Edward Island
Maximum assessable earnings per worker on which the payroll is reported: 82,900 in 2025, 89,300 in 2026.
Workers Compensation Board of Prince Edward Island

Coverage of the workers of most industries, with excluded occupations and industries that may buy optional coverage; proprietors and partners of non-incorporated businesses, independent operators and owners and directors of a corporation are covered only by voluntary personal coverage.
Workers Compensation Board of Prince Edward Island

Registration with one or more workers; renewal by February 28 with the actual payroll of the previous year and the estimate of the current year; payment within 30 days of the statement, semi-annual for an estimate filed by February 28 and an assessment of 1,000 or more, or monthly (MAPO) on the actual payroll of the previous month; 1.5% a month on overdue balances.
Workers Compensation Board of Prince Edward Island
Registration renewal by February 28, premiums by March 31, deferred payments by August 31 and payroll revisions by November 1.
Workers Compensation Act, RSPEI 1988, c. W-7.1
Sections 46 and 47 (maximum annual earnings); consolidation current to May 29, 2026

Maximum annual earnings since January 1, 2024: the Prince Edward Island average weekly earnings (industrial aggregate) at June 30 of the previous year x 52 x 1.5, rounded to the nearest 100; earnings above it are disregarded.
